title: American Community Survey 2020–2024 5-year Data Profiles (DP02, DP03, DP04, DP05): Naples city, Florida
measures: Naples city: population 19,704 (±22); households 9,836; under 18 9.0%; 65+ 55.8% (±3.1); median age 67.3; language other than English at home (5+) 9.3% (±2.1); Spanish 3.8%; English less than 'very well' 4.1%; bachelor's+ 64.3%; median household income $153,182 (±$25,425); mean commute 22.4 min (±8.3); uninsured 3.7%; owner-occupied 82.1%. Companion tables DP02/DP03/DP04 at the same geography.
limitations: ACS 5-year period estimates with margins of error; not a point-in-time count. Values retrieved through the data.census.gov table API (scripts/census.mjs). Small population: several margins are wide (income, commute).

title: American Community Survey 2020–2024 5-year Data Profiles (DP02, DP03, DP04, DP05): Tallahassee city, Florida
measures: Tallahassee city: population 201,875; households 85,311; under 18 16.6%; 65+ 11.7%; median age 28.2; language other than English 12.4%; Spanish 5.4%; median household income $57,409 (±$2,189); mean commute 19.1 min; uninsured 7.8%; owner-occupied 40.6%; government workers 29.1% (±1.4) of employed civilians (DP03 class of worker); public administration 12.9% (industry); educational services, health care and social assistance 28.4%; residents 3+ enrolled in college or graduate school 50,690 (±1,628); SNAP households 12.8%.
limitations: ACS 5-year period estimates with margins of error; not a point-in-time count. Values retrieved through the data.census.gov table API (scripts/census.mjs).

title: American Community Survey 2020–2024 5-year Data Profiles (DP02, DP03, DP04, DP05): Gainesville city, Florida
measures: Gainesville city: population 145,702; households 59,816; under 18 13.1%; 65+ 11.9%; median age 26.5; language other than English 18.2%; Spanish 8.8%; English less than 'very well' 3.1%; median household income $46,195 (±$2,205); mean commute 18.8 min; uninsured 7.4%; owner-occupied 37.7%; educational services, health care and social assistance 39.9% of employed (industry); government workers 29.2%; residents 3+ enrolled in college or graduate school 50,972 (±1,464) of 65,559 enrolled in school.

title: American Community Survey 2020–2024 5-year Data Profiles (DP02, DP03, DP04, DP05): Port St. Lucie city, Florida
measures: Port St. Lucie city: population 232,491; households 83,952; under 18 20.4%; 65+ 21.8%; median age 43.9; language other than English 26.7% (±1.5); Spanish 17.4% (±1.0); English less than 'very well' 8.6%; bachelor's+ 28.1%; median household income $80,648 (±$2,686); mean commute 30.5 min (±0.8); uninsured 10.3%; owner-occupied 84.0%.
limitations: ACS 5-year period estimates with margins of error; not a point-in-time count. Values retrieved through the data.census.gov table API (scripts/census.mjs). The 5-year population is a period average and is lower than the July 2025 point estimate; do not subtract them.

title: American Community Survey 2020–2024 5-year Data Profiles (DP02, DP03, DP04, DP05): Naples-Marco Island, Port St. Lucie, Tallahassee and Gainesville metro areas and their central counties
geography: Four Florida metro areas (2023 OMB delineations) and St. Lucie, Martin, Leon and Alachua counties
measures: Naples-Marco Island MSA (Collier County): population 398,291; under 18 16.3%; 65+ 33.8%; median age 53.3; language other than English 32.7%; Spanish 23.4%; English less than 'very well' 12.8%; median household income $90,045; uninsured 11.3%; mean commute 26.1. Port St. Lucie MSA: 522,676; 65+ 26.9%; median age 47.6; Spanish 14.4%; income $74,514; uninsured 11.1%; commute 29.0. St. Lucie County: 360,500; 65+ 24.6%; Spanish 15.9%. Martin County: 162,176; 65+ 32.2%; median age 53.3. Tallahassee MSA: 391,730; median age 34.8; 65+ 15.9%; income $65,261; uninsured 8.4%. Leon County: 297,542; median age 32.0. Gainesville MSA: 349,923; median age 34.5; income $61,468; uninsured 8.4%. Alachua County: 285,492; median age 32.3; income $61,949.
limitations: ACS 5-year period estimates with margins of error; not a point-in-time count. Values retrieved through the data.census.gov table API (scripts/census.mjs).

title: ACS 2020–2024 5-year, Table B25004 Vacancy Status and Table B25001 Housing Units: Naples, Port St. Lucie, Tallahassee and Gainesville
geography: Naples, Port St. Lucie, Tallahassee and Gainesville cities; Collier, St. Lucie and Martin counties
measures: Vacant units held for seasonal, recreational or occasional use as a share of all housing units (B25004_006 / B25001_001), calculated by Alpha Dental Media: Naples city 7,707 of 18,902 (40.8%); Collier County 59,512 of 239,406 (24.9%); Port St. Lucie city 4,160 of 90,911 (4.6%); St. Lucie County 15,319 of 160,146 (9.6%); Martin County 10,252 of 83,121 (12.3%); Tallahassee city 1,014 of 97,245 (1.0%); Gainesville city 185 of 66,114 (0.3%).
limitations: Counts housing units, not people; a proxy for part-year presence only. Margins of error apply to numerators.

title: ACS 2020–2024 5-year, Table B08007 Sex of Workers by Place of Work (State and County of Residence): four Florida cities
geography: Port St. Lucie, Tallahassee, Gainesville and Naples cities, Florida
measures: Workers 16+ living in each city by whether they work in their county of residence: Port St. Lucie 104,063 workers, 64,820 in St. Lucie County, 37,839 (36.4%) outside the county; Tallahassee 104,284, 98,531 in county, 4,509 outside (4.3%); Gainesville 68,536, 64,662 in county, 3,097 outside (4.5%); Naples 6,164, 5,378 in county. Shares calculated by Alpha Dental Media.
limitations: Place of work for the main job in the reference week; does not show commute direction or destination county.

title: Subcounty Resident Population Estimates: April 1, 2020 to July 1, 2025 (SUB-EST2025, all states file)
publisher: U.S. Census Bureau, Population Estimates Program
measures: Estimates base April 2020 and July 1 estimates 2020–2025 for Florida places and counties: Port St. Lucie city 204,826 → 268,062 (+30.9%; +9,131 in 2024–25); St. Lucie County 329,226 → 402,449 (+22.2%); Martin County 158,432 → 166,272 (+4.9%); Naples city 19,126 → 20,114 (+5.2%; 20,214 in 2024); Marco Island city 16,421 (2025); Collier County 375,763 → 417,131 (+11.0%); Tallahassee city 196,182 → 204,902 (+4.4%); Leon County 292,205 → 299,048; Gainesville city 141,161 → 148,671 (+5.3%); Alachua County 278,478 → 290,028; Florida 21,538,207 → 23,462,518 (+8.9%). Rankings among 26 Florida cities of 100,000+ (calculated): Port St. Lucie highest percentage growth, second-largest numeric gain after Jacksonville, fifth-most-populous in 2025.
limitations: Resident (usual-residence) estimates; they do not count seasonal presence. Estimates are revised each vintage.

title: List 1: Core Based Statistical Areas, Metropolitan Divisions and Combined Statistical Areas, July 2023 (Florida entries)
measures: County composition: Naples-Marco Island, FL MSA (34940) = Collier County, within the Cape Coral-Fort Myers-Naples CSA; Port St. Lucie, FL MSA (38940) = Martin and St. Lucie counties, within the Miami-Port St. Lucie-Fort Lauderdale CSA; Tallahassee, FL MSA (45220) = Leon (central), Gadsden, Jefferson, Wakulla; Gainesville, FL MSA (23540) = Alachua (central), Gilchrist, Levy, within the Gainesville-Lake City CSA.
limitations: Statistical definitions; they do not describe patient travel.

title: Florida State University 2025–2026 Pocket Fact Book
publisher: Florida State University Office of Institutional Research
measures: Fall 2025 enrollment 46,184 (71.6% undergraduate, 23.9% graduate/professional); 80.0% Floridians; average age 22.9; Leon County among 18 Florida counties contributing 500+ students; 80.5% full-time.
limitations: University-wide headcount (all campuses and online students), not a count of Tallahassee residents.

title: UF Facts
measures: Enrollment as of fall 2025: 41,109 undergraduate, 2,023 non-degree undergraduate, 14,894 graduate, 4,184 professional, total 63,148; in-state 47,028, out-of-state 16,120; 33,516 employees including 6,195 faculty (fall 2025).
limitations: University-wide figures including online students; not Gainesville resident counts. Page also contains promotional rankings, which are not used.

title: Forever Smiles South
publisher: Florida Department of Health in St. Lucie County
geography: Port St. Lucie, St. Lucie County, Florida

limitations: Small, non-random sample found with an unordered web-search tool; static HTML may omit script-loaded features; describes websites, not practice performance.
